name: Krsnananda Agamavagisa
dates_notes: A Bengali Śākta compiler conventionally placed around 1575–1600; the exact biographical dates remain uncertain.
core_thesis: Kṛṣṇānanda Āgamavāgīśa is associated with the *Bṛhat-Tantrasāra*, a large early-modern Bengali Sanskrit digest of Tantric sources. Its contribution is chiefly editorial and systematic: it selects, orders, and transmits a wide body of ritual, mantra, and doctrinal material across Śākta and related Tantric traditions. The record treats the digest as evidence for early-modern organization and reception, not as evidence that all of its cited materials share one doctrine or historical origin.

engaged_works.title: Brhat-Tantrasara
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Standardly transmitted as Kṛṣṇānanda Āgamavāgīśa's Tantric digest.
engaged_works.summary: An encyclopedic early-modern Tantric digest that compiles and organizes material on ritual, mantra, worship, and allied technical topics. Printed editions exist, including editions in Bengali script; passage-level interpretation should await a verified local text witness.
